Listeners on #searchInput are keydown, focus and input. works.md line 247 says the portal's article search shows suggestions. confirmed.suspectedCause: The portal's typeahead probably builds its dropdown on the field's 'focus' event. Sift keeps the page inert and replays only input, so focus never reaches the page field. Lead: send a focus event to the page field when the user enters Sift's field.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 2 of 2 with Sift on, typing 'Pumper' and 'Baguette' into Sift's 'Search Wikipedia' field on www.wikipedia.org. Sift showed 0 suggestions and the page made no .suggestions-dropdown, even though the page field held the value. The page's JSONP query did fire (#api_opensearch script present). The control with Sift off (real click in #searchInput, type 'Pumper') gave a 427 px dropdown with 6 links. The suspected cause is wrong. The portal's focus and input listeners are the same 100 ms debounced query, and its render callback (portalOpensearchCallback) draws only `if (document.activeElement === searchInput)`. With Sift on, document.activeElement is sift-root. Sift's activeElement shim in src/main/index.ts only applies after a 'sift-enter', and proxy.focus() sends that only for fields matching [role=combobox], [aria-autocomplete], [aria-controls], [aria-owns] or [list]. The portal's #searchInput has none of these (type=search, autocomplete=off). works.md line 247 says this worked in round 6, so the regression claim is consistent.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/proxy.ts focus(), also send 'sift-enter' for plain search fields (input[type=search], [role=searchbox], or a text input inside a search form or role=search), so the activeElement shim in src/main/index.ts names the page field. Alternatively, apply the shim to any text field Sift has entered.

confirmed.suspectedCause: After the last keystroke, Sift extracts once before the page's list fills (or skips the run). No later mutation brings the sheet up until another input event. Possibly the new suggestAt fast path in index.ts's mutation observer, or the typedRun timer: schedule(...lastRunAt + max(100, lastDur*2) - now).
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced as a lasting sync failure. Unthrottled at low load it passed 4 of 4. Unthrottled at load average 12-22 it failed 1 of 4 and 1 of 1. With renderer CPU throttling via CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate, which simulates a slower machine, it failed 3 of 3 at 2x, 2 of 2 at 3x, 3 of 3 at 4x and 4 of 5 at 6x. In every failure the page's #searchform menu held 11 options with aria-expanded=true and the value typed. Sift's sheet stayed at 0 buttons at 3, 8 and 18 s, and still 5 s after throttling was removed. host.dataset.runs shows Sift ran an extraction after the list filled (6 to 7), so runs happened but produced no sheet. In the slow runs the page had not yet swapped #searchInput for the Codex typeahead input when typing ended: at 3 s the input was still searchInput with no aria-controls; later it was an input with aria-controls=v-0. document.activeElement stayed sift-root, so no sift-enter took effect. This points to Sift's ref still naming the old, removed field. fieldList() uses elOf(a.dataset.ref), which returns null for a disconnected element, so it returns undefined. Only the next keystroke adopts the new field, via input() calling liveField(), which matches the report that one more key shows the list.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/index.ts fieldList(), resolve the page field with liveField(a.dataset.ref, false) instead of elOf(), so a swapped-in field (Wikipedia's typeahead) is adopted at the next run. Also, in the 'sift-focus' handler, adopt the new field even when the old one is still connected at the moment of the page's focus() call. Then send proxy.focus/sift-enter to the adopted field.

So in the Short version the byline sits in the middle of the post, and the code example appears after it with nothing explaining it. Block counts are still right (blockquotes 6/6, pre 3/3). confirmed.suspectedCause: The Short version replaces the post's prose but leaves the header row and the non-prose blocks (pre, link preview) where they were, after the shortened text. The question that introduced the code is dropped by the model.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on github.com/preactjs/preact/issues/4416 (shot research/shots/skeptic-gh4416.png). The Short version reads 'SHORT VERSION / Show full text', 5 short paragraphs, then 'trusktr', 'opened on Jun 20, 2024', then the pre 'return <some-element foo={[1, 2, 3]} />', then the custom-elements-everywhere link. Sift's own full text starts with 'trusktr / opened on Jun 20, 2024', and the code follows 'Does this set an attribute, or a property?'. So in the Short version the post's byline sits after its text, as if starting a new post, and the code example sits under it with nothing introducing it. These blocks are kept-whole placeholders ([[B…]]) in src/content/short.ts. planShort() trusts where the model put them and re-places only dropped ones by source position. A leading byline therefore drifts to wherever the model wrote its placeholder.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/short.ts planShort(), keep kept-whole blocks that come before the first prose unit (a post's header row or byline) pinned in front, rather than placing them where the model wrote them. When a placeholder comes out of source order, re-place it by its source position with the same anchor logic used for dropped units. This keeps the code block after the shortened sentence that introduced it, or the model can be asked to keep that sentence.
